analysis.step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core data ingest sources on the left side: On-Premise datacenter (OnPremDC) and AWS cloud logs container. Per Rule 4 (Mandatory Decomposition of Grouped Boxes), the 'AWS' box is decomposed into explicitly named AWS services: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, SNS, SQS.
2. Ingested events flow into Apache Metron (ThirdParty) for real-time parsing, profiling, and enrichment.
3. In the center, Apache Metron streams persistent data into the Security Data Lake container, connecting to EMR, which writes transformed data to S3, queried by Athena. A feedback loop exists from S3 back to Apache Metron to update contextual intelligence.
4. On the right side, alerts from Apache Metron flow to the SOAR platform (ThirdParty), which sends alerts to SOC Analysts (UserCompanyAnalyst). Analysts take remediation actions via WAF.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows an automated server migration solution from On-Premises to AWS built by Versant. On-Premises infrastructure sends metadata to AWS Application Discovery Service and block-level data replication directly to an EC2 Hot Replica. The Migration Team interacts via Slack (triggering the Migration Factory running on an EC2 instance) and inputs operational metadata into DynamoDB. The central Migration Factory EC2 instance orchestrates the flow: querying App Discovery Service, interacting with CloudEndure to stop replication on the EC2 Hot Replica, baking an AMI, sharing that AMI across account boundaries to the target account, and launching the target EC2 instance in the target account.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram displays Sunday Sky's Rendering as a Service (RaaS) platform on AWS. 1) Client devices (UserConsumerWebMobile) initiate requests through Amazon API Gateway, which forwards to a Frontend Lambda function. 2) The Frontend Lambda validates the request and places rendering instructions in an SQS queue. 3) EC2 Auto Scaling instances pull rendering jobs from the SQS queue, process them, and send job status/playlist info back to a second SQS queue, which the Frontend Lambda reads from to return a playlist URL to the Client. 4) Processed video segments are stored in S3 by the EC2 Auto Scaling workers, and delivered to users via CloudFront. 5) Scaling is managed via AWS Step Functions triggering a Scaling Lambda that interacts with the EC2 Auto Scaling group. 6) Spot instance interruptions are handled by CloudWatch Events triggering an Interruption Lambda, which signals the affected EC2 instance to drain jobs and detach from the Auto Scaling group.
